issue_context.title: `Dataframe.sample()` isn't validating `frac`
issue_context.body:
Minor/trivial bug:

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/core/generic.py#L4960

Shouldn't `sample()` check that `frac` is between 0 and 1 somewhere?

Doc improvement suggestion:

Could anyone confirm that `replace=True|False` means allowing|disallowing sampling the same row more than once?

Methinks the docs could use an update to make what `replace` does clearer for newcomers - or at least for those who aren't familiar with `numpy`.
comments:
> Shouldn't `sample()` check that `frac` is between 0 and 1 somewhere?

We don't want to restrict the upper bound of `frac` because we allow oversampling when sampling with replacement.  Also note that validation is performed against the resulting `n` that's derived from `frac` for cases where an invalid `frac` is passed:

```python
In [2]: df = pd.DataFrame({'A': list('abc')})

In [3]: df.sample(frac=2, replace=True)
Out[3]: 
   A
1  b
0  a
1  b
2  c
2  c
2  c

In [4]: df.sample(frac=2, replace=False)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ValueError: Cannot take a larger sample than population when 'replace=False'

In [5]: df.sample(frac=-0.5)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ValueError: A negative number of rows requested. Please provide positive value.
```

> Could anyone confirm that replace=True|False means allowing|disallowing sampling the same row more than once?

Correct.

> Methinks the docs could use an update to make what `replace` does clearer for newcomers - or at least for those who aren't familiar with `numpy`.

Improvements to the docs are always welcome!

@jschendel I've created a pull request to fix the doc issue and add a check for `frac <= 0`. No idea what the three items that are missing are about, but given the change I presume they'll all pass so I'll let you pick it up from here.

review_comments: Can you add an example to the Examples section of the docstring where this is used in a meaningful way? Specifically where rows are resampled, as the current example with `replace=True` doesn't actually show this behavior.

doctest failure: https://dev.azure.com/pandas-dev/pandas/_build/results?buildId=14665

Do you get this output locally? You may need to play with random_state to get an outcome we want.

Yes, that's what I got when playing around with the example data frame in `sample()`. I purposefully kept the same `random_state=1` and increased `n` until I got a dup. (If you'd rather only 2 rows, use `random_state=4` with `n=2`.)
Ah, sorry it's actually L4879 (the `df.sample(frac=0.5, random_state=1)`) that needs to be updated now that `replace=False` there

I don't think we actually need to explicitly write this check since, as shown in the issue, this validation already occurs after an `n` is computed from `frac` (conversion in the `elif` below this one, negative check a few lines below that).

It is interesting that this didn't cause the test suite to fail, as we check the messages associated with the errors.   That probably means we don't have a test for the `frac < 0` case, so would be nice to add one.
